region: Cultural Triangle, Wilpattu, Hill Country and Udawalawe
title: Sri Lanka — Sacred Cities, Leopard Lakes and the Tea Escarpment
subtitle: Thirteen days from Anuradhapura's stupas to Ella's railway, with leopards at dawn
summary: A 13-day loop through Buddhist capitals, Wilpattu and Udawalawe safaris and the Kandy-to-Ella tea hills, with a driver-guide and a highland train. Rich in culture and wildlife but fuel quotas, cyclone damage to rail and tuk-tuk licence rules need checking.
introduction: Start in the drylands north of Colombo with a night in a tented camp beside Wilpattu's lake-studded forest and a dawn jeep search for leopards. Cycle between Anuradhapura's white stupas, climb Mihintale before sunrise, walk the ruined forest monastery of Ritigala, then ascend Sigiriya and cycle Polonnaruwa's Gal Vihara Buddhas. Drive into Kandy for the Tooth Relic puja, climb through tea estates to Nuwara Eliya, ride the highland train to Ella, hike Ella Rock and watch Lipton's Seat at dusk. Finish with elephants at Udawalawe. Two travellers drive nothing: a driver-guide handles roads and fuel.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is empty desert and self-contained driving; this route is dense with living Buddhism, 2,000-year-old capitals, rail and tea estates, and relies on a driver because roads, fuel quotas and licence rules make four-person self-drive less attractive. Camping is limited to organised sites, not wild desert camps.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: The standard circuit stacks Sigiriya, Kandy and Ella on air-conditioned schedules. This one adds Wilpattu leopard country, Ritigala's forest monastery, Mihintale at dawn, bicycle days in the sacred cities and homestays, and keeps the group flexible through two buffer days.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: Sri Lanka alone combines a continuous 2,000-year Buddhist royal history, leopards and elephants, and a scenic highland railway in one short loop. Culture, wildlife and tea landscapes sit within 4 h drives of each other, with a small budget footprint compared with long-haul Asian peers.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: February is the driest and coolest part of the dry season in the Cultural Triangle and hill country, Wilpattu is in its dry-season leopard window, and the Udawalawe elephants are resident year-round. March heat rises and afternoon thunderstorms begin from mid-March. The window ends on Navam Poya (Sat 20 Feb 2027, listed by Office Holidays), so book the final transfer early; Ramadan starts around 8 Feb with little effect on a Buddhist-majority route.

februarySuitability.summary: Dry in the dry-zone and hill country, warm and sunny, good for the train and hikes; Poya on 20 Feb brings crowds at shrines.

marchSuitability.summary: Hotter (30–34 C in the dry zone), thunderstorms from mid-March, but still workable; Gal Oya boat safaris and Medin Poya (about 22 Mar) are possible additions.

geography.summary: Dry-zone plains with ancient reservoirs and rock outcrops rise through Kandy's basin into 2,000 m tea highlands before falling to elephant grassland.
geography.distinctive: Within 200 km: leopard lakes of Wilpattu, a 200-m granite plug at Sigiriya, 1,900 m tea plateau at Nuwara Eliya and an escarpment edge at Haputale looking over the southern plains.

travelStyle.summary: A driver-guide in a van for the long legs, with trains, bicycles, jeeps and walking on top; two nights in organised camps and the rest in guesthouses/homestays.

transport.summary: Roads are slow, with erratic driving and accidents; fuel purchases were capped in 2026 though tourism operators received a special allowance. A van with driver is the realistic backbone; use the Nanu Oya–Ella train and local tuk-tuks with drivers.

modes.description: Private air-conditioned van and driver for 11 days; the realistic scenario. Drivers know roads, fuel and parking, and carry bags between train legs.
Two licensed travellers drive a rented car with a Sri Lankan recognition permit. Possible but tiring on narrow, crowded roads.
Reserved seats; service restored 20 Jun 2026; Kandy–Nanu Oya and Colombo–Kandy sections still being repaired in Sept 2026.
For short hops inside Anuradhapura, Polonnaruwa and Ella; agree fare before riding.
Cheap but crowded, and FCDO notes public buses are often driven fast and poorly maintained; avoid for luggage-heavy legs.

transport.carRental: Self-drive rental exists but is uncommon: most visitors hire a driver. Rental firms usually help arrange the recognition permit. Check minimum age, deposit, additional-driver rules, insurance excess and fuel-quota status before booking. One-way fees not verified.

drivingRequirements.summary: Legal self-drive needs a valid full licence, a physical 1949 IDP and a Sri Lankan recognition permit (AA Ceylon) or a DMT temporary licence from Colombo airport. Only the two licensed travellers may drive. Road safety is poor, so a hired driver is the recommended approach.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: A 1949-Convention IDP, issued at home, is needed alongside the home licence; digital IDPs are reportedly refused. Applicability depends on licence country, which is not assumed here.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences; the other two may not drive any vehicle. Recognition permit about USD 40 per rental-industry guides; DMT airport licence reported since Aug 2025 and excludes tuk-tuks and heavy vehicles.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No one may ride motorcycles, scooters or tuk-tuks without a licence for that class. Self-drive tuk-tuk rental is legally contested: police HQ said IDP holders may not drive three-wheelers (Nov 2025), a Court of Appeal interim order in Feb 2026 restored the earlier position, DMT says a local test is required for a tuk-tuk licence, and the final ruling was not found. The two unlicensed travellers cannot drive in any case; the plan rides tuk-tuks with local drivers only.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Hire a van with driver-guide for the whole land route (also solves fuel quotas), use trains and bicycles, and leave self-drive and any tuk-tuk driving off the plan unless the AAC/DMT/rental company confirm in writing before booking.

accommodation.summary: Guesthouses and homestays in Anuradhapura, Sigiriya, Kandy, Ella and Haputale; hotel in Nuwara Eliya; two organised tented camps; Negombo guesthouse for the last night.

camping.summary: Camping is mostly via organised campsites near parks (Wilpattu, Udawalawe) with tents supplied; wild camping is not recommended and park rules and permits were not verified.

physicalDifficulty.label: moderate
physicalDifficulty.summary: Heat, stairs at Sigiriya and Mihintale and a 3–4 h Ella Rock hike are the main efforts; driving is passive.

itinerary.summary: A 13-day loop from Colombo through Wilpattu, the Cultural Triangle, Kandy, the highland railway and Udawalawe, using a van with driver and bicycles on site days.

security.summary: No assessed authority advises against travel to any part of the route; France places the whole country in 'vigilance renforcée' and Australia asks for a high degree of caution. Terrorism cannot be excluded after 2019, and the northern and eastern provinces (not on the route) still contain mines.
security.assessedRoute: Colombo–Wilpattu–Anuradhapura–Mihintale–Ritigala–Sigiriya–Polonnaruwa–Kandy–Nuwara Eliya–Ella–Haputale–Udawalawe–Negombo (North Western, North Central, Central, Uva and Southern provinces). Jaffna, Mullaitivu, Mannar and the east coast are excluded from the plan.
